Gramlot 0.2.14 writes the client/server contract down and realises it: one envelope over one URL, two gramlot-content-types, endpoints, `auth` closed by default, and the `dataRpc` data-element.

## What changes

- One URL, one envelope: the client sends `{id, pageId, contentType, name, params}` as TYTX JSON text to `POST /gramlot/rpc`, which replaces `/gramlot/main` and `/gramlot/source`. `contentType` is `source` (a fragment of Source; the whole page is the fragment named `main`) or `data` (a value from an endpoint). The response is `{id, contentType, value}` or `{id, contentType, error: {code, name, message}}`; outcomes are `page_expired`, `not_found`, `not_authenticated`, `not_authorized`, `application_error`. HTTP status codes are left to transport failures. `POST /gramlot/close` with `{pageId}` is unchanged.
- `GramlotServer.call(text, owner)` (Python `call(text, *, owner=None)`, JS `call(text, {owner})`) answers the envelope and raises only `InvalidRequest`; `main` and `source` are gone. Options `rpc_url` / `rpcUrl` replace `main_url`+`source_url` / `mainUrl`+`sourceUrl`; the bootstrap config is `{pageId, rpcUrl, closeUrl, rootId, capabilities}`.
- Endpoints: Python `@endpoint` and `@endpoint(auth="rule")`, JS `Page.registerEndpoint('name', {auth})`; `@source` / `registerSource` take the same `auth`. The base evaluator `evaluate_auth` / `evaluateAuth` knows no identity and answers `not_authenticated` to any rule; a server with the `auth` capability overrides it. The element-side exclusion in the builders is gramlot-org/gramlot#34.
- Client: `HttpTransport` replaces `MainTransport`; `gramlot.rpc.call(contentType, name, params)` sends the envelope and rejects with `RpcError` (`code`, `remoteName`, `message`); `main` and remote fragments go through it.
- `dataRpc(method, result_path=None, timeout=None)` enters the grammar and the binding: the Provider pipeline (`_if`, `_delay`, `_timing`, `_userChanges`, …), latest call wins per node, `timeout` in milliseconds, inline `_onCalling` / `_onResult` / `_onError`, a `dataRpc` child of a `button` runs on click. `dataRemote` and the `remote` attribute stay excluded.
- No request size limit in the contract; `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` and the mandatory 413 are gone from the reference adapters.
- GC-230 is the contract (Part A) with its HTTP, Worker and WebSocket realisations; `check_protocol` / `checkProtocol` run its 16-item list, now with a typed value through `call`. GC-095 §100 documents `dataRpc` and endpoints; constitution amendment 11.58 records the contract.

## Upgrading from 0.2.12

- Adapters: route `POST /gramlot/rpc` to `call(body_text, owner)`, answer 200 with its text, 400 on `InvalidRequest`; drop the `main`/`source` routes and the size limit; rename the URL options.
- Pages: declare endpoints with `@endpoint` / `registerEndpoint`; a Python endpoint called from `dataRpc` declares `**kwargs`.
- Client code that imported `MainTransport` imports `HttpTransport`; test fakes implement `call(text, signal)`.
- gramlot-js-server, gramlot-py-server and gramlot-examples are released together with this version.
